gateCatches.finding: F-5: the F-2 fix reproduced the F-1 defect it sat beside — create() read vnode.tag three times (typeof, Set.has, createElement), so a stateful getter or Proxy validated as 'div' and constructed 'script'. Not reachable in this build; sent back so precondition 7.1 could be struck honestly rather than recorded as a guarantee the code did not provide.

notes.overrunReason: A bad estimate, not a missing check. The pre-spawn check ran before all five spawns and passed every time. Two of the five estimates were invented rather than drawn from RUN_ECONOMICS.md §1: the `smoke` rework (est 50k, actual 73k) and the resumed Security re-verify (est 40k, actual 115k). The re-verify was priced cheap on the reasoning that a SendMessage-resumed agent with intact context would be cheap — wrong, because a resumed agent still re-processes accumulated context every turn, and because the re-verify did substantial new work (Proxy trap-count probes, reconstructed pre-rework source, a three-mutant mutation test). It cost a review stage because it was one. The four estimates that DID come from the archetype table were accurate to within 14k.
notes.recordedAs: UNAUTHORIZED overrun — distinct from browser-client, where the Orchestrator stopped at the pre-spawn check and the human approved the exception. Here the check passed on a bad number, so the human was never asked. The 490k budget stands; it was not raised to fit the spend.
proposedProtocolAmendments: Add a fourth archetype: `re-gate` ~100k. A re-gate is a review stage whether spawned cold or resumed; SendMessage resumption is a quality/latency optimisation, not a cost one.

Price rework by verification surface, not diff size — a one-line fix cost 73k because reading the finding, re-deriving fail-first, and re-running gates do not scale with line count. Suggested `smoke` rework floor ~75k.
Make `no archetype fits` an escalation: record in STATE.md that an estimate is unfounded BEFORE spawning, and widen headroom rather than picking a number that happens to fit.

notes.leastPrivilegeNote: Orchestrator session rooted in the product repo, so .claude/agents/ was discoverable and all five spawns used the generated agents with tools: frontmatter in force (Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob). Closes the carry-forward from runs/browser-client/STATE.md. The boundary bound: QA and Security had no browser tool and drove headless Chrome over CDP from Bash via Node 25's native WebSocket, dependency-free; Security's re-verify ran entirely in-process against a stub document, opening no port. The stub-document probe is what found F-5 — it counts property reads and Proxy trap invocations, which a real browser cannot see.
